title: Gold's Decline: Fed Rate Hike Prospects and Your Investments
description: Stronger-than-expected US payrolls data has increased the likelihood of an interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve. This expectation has led to a decline.

faq.q: What is a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike?
faq.a: A Fed rate hike refers to the US central bank increasing its benchmark interest rate, known as the federal funds rate. This makes borrowing more expensive and saving more attractive, aiming to cool down the economy and control inflation.

faq.q: Why does the US jobs report matter for gold?
faq.a: A strong US jobs report indicates a healthy economy, which can prompt the Fed to raise interest rates to prevent inflation. Higher interest rates typically make non-yielding assets like gold less attractive, leading to a decline in its price.

faq.q: Does a strong US dollar affect gold prices?
faq.a: Yes, a strong US dollar generally puts downward pressure on gold prices. Since gold is primarily priced in dollars, a stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for international buyers using other currencies, reducing demand.

faq.q: How do I invest in gold in India?
faq.a: You can invest in gold in India through various avenues: physical gold (jewellery, coins, bars), Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), Gold Mutual Funds, and Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) issued by the RBI.

faq.q: Should I sell my gold now due to the decline?
faq.a: Deciding whether to sell gold depends on your individual financial goals, risk tolerance, and investment horizon. Gold is often considered a long-term hedge against inflation and currency depreciation. Short-term price fluctuations due to macro events are common.

Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are government securities denominated in grams of gold. They are substitutes for holding physical gold, offering benefits like an annual interest rate (2.50% p.a. currently) and tax exemptions on capital gains if held till maturity.

based_on.title: Gold Holds Decline as Traders Weigh Prospects for Fed Rate Hike
